newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - April 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday issued a strong warning that excessively large enterprise bargaining pay deals could bring on an inflationary upsurge. Costello's warning came as Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showed a rise of just 0.2 percent in the consumer price index, and an inflation rate of 1.3 percent, the lowest in four years. Page 1.

As the federal government discusses its cross-media ownership rules, Opposition Leader Kim Beazley has explicitly ruled out allowing Nine Network owner Kerry Packer to own John Fairfax newspaper group. Beazley said he objects to the "crushing of diversity" that would arise from the elimination of cross-media rules. Page 3.

Mackay Sugar last night launched a A$200 million damages claim against the Queensland Sugar Corp, throwing Australia's A$2 billion sugar industry into turmoil. The damages arise from allegations Queensland Sugar Corp gave preferential treatment to other customers and discriminated against Mackay. Page 23.

Maurice Romano, managing director of Australia's largest retail chemist chain, Amcal, said yesterday the company has decided against a plan to transfer its A$700 million in product purchases to a single preferred supplier. While Australian Pharmaceutical Industries was understood to have been frontrunner in the contract negotiations, Romano said Amcal felt it was better not to align itself with a wholesaler. Page 23.

Neither side would comment yesterday on the breakdown of negotiations between the manager and trustee, Meridian Investment Trust and parties associated with the former trustee of the Estate Mortgage trusts. The mediation conference ordered by Justice Smith, the judge in charge of the case currently in the Supreme Court of Victoria, has been suspended without resolution. Page 24.

After expressing interest in buying into the New South Wales TAB float, shares in Tabcorp Holdings surged yesterday on renewed hopes of a capital return to shareholders. The optimism comes as the New South Wales Government ruled out allowing gaming compaies to participate in the float. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp yesterday announced new government guidelines that will favour new entrants and airlines using their own aircraft on international routes rather than working under code-share arrangements. The guidelines will affect both Qantas and Ansett which are planning on expanding their international links using a combination of code-sharing and their own aircraft. Page 21.

Thanks to a near record rise on the U.S. sharemarket and confirmation that the Australian inflation remains low, the All Ordinaries jumped more than one percent yesterday, finishing at 2472.3. Investors were pleased with the consumer price index released yesterday which supported Australia's status as a low inflation country. Page 21.

Shares in Comalco Ltd rose yesterday after chairman Leigh Clifford's announcement to shareholders that the aluminium group was heading for improved earnings in 1997 thanks to stronger demand and increased prices. Clifford said reasonable results in the first quarter and early signs signalled a retention of the current performance levels. Page 21.

Comalco chairman and CRA managing director Leigh Clifford said yesterday the Federal Government must deliver certainty and clarity on native title. Clifford said that while many companies are happy to work with Aboriginal negotiators, the native title process failed to deliver quick, clear and certain agreement. Page 21.

Australian Resources Ltd is under new management and has received satisfactory drilling results from its three producing gold assets in Western Australia and Queensland, suggesting an expansion in annual production from 200,000 ounces to 400,000 ounces over the next few years. Page 22.

Acacia Resources chairman Peter Wade told the company's annual meeting in Melbourne yesterday gold production will be increased by 30 percent to over 350,000 ounces this year to recover from problems associated with heavy rains at the gold producer's Northern Territory operations. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Commonwealth Bank of Australia managing director David Murray said yesterday the adoption of the Wallis inquiry recommendation that all financial institutions that take deposits from the public be supervised by one mega-regulator, would risk a savings and loan scandal similar to that which cost American taxpayers billions of dollars and would reduce the Reserve Bank's ability to supervise. Page 31.

Following last month's decision to buy its partners out of the struggling Optus Vision joint venture, Optus Communications will meet today to decide the pay-TV operation's future. The meeting will include representatives from Optus' overseas shareholders Cable and Wireless and BellSouth, and must decide the future form of the company. Page 31.

New South Wales Minister for Fair Trading, Fay Lo Po, told State Parliament yesterday she was concerned at the current direction of changes in the banking industry and said customer complaints against banks, especially those from rural areas, will be addressed at a urgent meeting between the New South Wales Government and the state general managers of the big banks operating in the state. Page 31.

As investors reacted positively yesterday to the news Australia can now cement its reputation as a low inflation country, benchmark 10-year November 2006 Commonwealth Government bond yields were one basis point higher than the previous day's close at 7.81 percent. Page 31.

Corporate restructuring, including nine acquisitions in Australia and New Zealand in the year to March 1, led office supplies company Corporate Express Australia to suffer a net loss of A$5.95 million and a A$4.3 million abnormal loss. Corporate Express shares fell three cents to 97 cents. Page 33.

Former Bond Corp executive Tony Oates, awaiting extradition proceedings in Polish jail, is willing to pay his air fare to Perth to face charges of defrauding more than A$1 billion from Bell Resources. Oates' offer of return is under the condition that he be granted similar bail to that given to former Bond Corp executive Peter Mitchell, who kept his passport. Page 33.
THE AGE

The March quarter consumer price index, showing growth of just 0.2 percent and an annual figure of 1.3 percent, augured well for financial markets yesterday, with the All Ordinaries Index climbing over 24 points to 2471.7. The All Ords also benefited fom a Wall Street surge. Page B1.

It is suspected the 14.6 percent purchase of Australian upmarket retailer Country Road is from South Africa's Wooltru group, which controls fellow Australian fashion group Sportsgirl. Should the deal be confirmed, it will counterbalance the unwelcome nine percent holding in Country Road held by Soloman and Peter Lew. Page B1.

Pacific Dunlop senior legal counsel Martin Hudson confirmed yesterday claims against PacDun unit Accufix Research Institute over the broken leads in pacemakers made by the former Telectronics unit were settled privately. In the United States PacDun is facing hundreds of legal claims from patients who suffered medical problems from the broken leads. Page B1.

Federal Industry Minister John Moore told the Sydney Institute last night there needs to be a lowering of the overall tax burden and a review of the capital gains tax in order to boost investment. Moore said Australia would be able to attract further investment with lower wage costs, and claimed living conditions in Australia would improve if the decline in its share of world investment was reversed. Page B1.

A Papua New Guinea judicial inquiry heard yesterday that sacked defence force commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok sent a confidential memo to then Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, asking RTZ-CRA to secretly finance military operations on Bougainville through the reopening of the Panguna mine. However, a CRA spokesman said yesterday that CRA received no such approach and that it never supported the use of mercenaries on Bougainville. Page B3.

Perth-based BankWest announced a A$94.5 million net profit yesterday which fell well short of forecasts. Chairman Ian Mackenzie said earnings dropped thanks to increased competition in the home-lending market, where interest rates margins narrowed sigificantly in the second half. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
